name: MBWF World Championship
epitaph: The league's top belt, open to men, and vacant when the league opened on 10 October 1992; Death Croc was champion by 19 October. Wolverine took it from him at Friday Ferocity #2 on 26 February 1993 and lost it back to him at Grapple Wars on 18 June 1993.
notes: Named in the league's founding post ("M.B.W.F. World Champion"), its update of 19 October 1992, the newsletter of 18 March 1993 and Grapple Wars 1; "World Heavyweight Champion.... Men Only" in its write-up of 14 December 1993.

name: MBWF Ladies World Championship
epitaph: The ladies' league's singles belt. The Countess, the first woman to enter the league, was champion by default until Angel Pit Bull beat her at Grapple Wars on 18 June 1993.
notes: "Ladies World Champion......... Ladies Only" in the league's write-up of 14 December 1993.

name: MBWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Open to men's and ladies' teams. Tempest, the first team entered, were the first champions; the Slammers held the belts by 14 June 1993 and lost them to Pain Unbound at Grapple Wars on 18 June 1993 after one of their own stopped fighting for the other.
notes: "World Tag Team Champions...... Mens teams and Ladies Teams" in the league's write-up of 14 December 1993.

name: MBWF Air Wave Championship
epitaph: A men's belt first won by the Electric Youth at the league's Winter Bash of 1992, with a defence due within 28 days; he was still champion when he beat Scourge at Grapple Wars on 18 June 1993.
notes: "Air Wave Champion............. Men Only" in the league's write-up of 14 December 1993.

name: MBWF Master of the Ring Championship
epitaph: A men's belt that the Gross Gladiator took from Scourge on 30 November 1992 on a Monday Madness show, with a defence due within 14 days, and kept until the Great Tadaka pinned him at Grapple Wars on 18 June 1993.
notes: "Master of the Ring............ Men Only" in the league's write-up of 14 December 1993.

name: MBWF All-Comers Championship
epitaph: Open to men and ladies and decided by a sixteen-man tournament that was set to open on 23 April 1993. Colossus won its final from Noose Lupack at Grapple Wars on 18 June 1993 and was its first champion.
notes: "All-Comers Champion........... Men and Ladies" in the league's write-up of 14 December 1993.

name: MBWF Princess of the Ring Championship
epitaph: A ladies' belt named in the league's write-up of December 1993. No holder is named.
notes: "Princess of the Ring.......... Ladies Only" in the league's write-up of 14 December 1993.
